_status: Re-read 2026-09-16 against the six-view renders (the two bottom obliques added 2026-09-01 included): every call below stands. The board prints values and the KF301 part number, no designators, and the two bottom obliques show the same bare copper side as view_bottom -- no pin-1 cue appears at an angle that was hidden straight-on. Originally written from the four-view renders; the per-component evidence is unchanged.
_rule: Anything absent defaults to NOT observable. Marking may only ever weaken the target: an unreadable value stops being scored, indistinguishable terminals merge into one class. See docs/METRIC.md.
_render: view_top, view_bottom, view_top_obl_a, view_top_obl_b, view_bottom_obl_a, view_bottom_obl_b
_terminal_identity_note: Every component is marked terminal_identity:false, and that is a considered call rather than a shortcut. Neither polarised part carries a package-level orientation cue in these renders: C2's can is plain with no polarity band, and U1's KF301 body is symmetric top-to-bottom with no pin-1 dot. A reader CAN tell U1's two pads apart in view_bottom — one has thermal-relief spokes into the GND pour, the other a solid isolation ring — but that is evidence about CONNECTIVITY, not about which pad the source calls pin 1. With sigma free the pairing is still scored: putting one pad on GND and the other on V+ earns both incidences, putting both on GND earns one. Forcing sigma would instead demand the agent guess the source's pin numbering from a board that never prints it.

C1.why: view_top: silkscreen '100nF' immediately left of the 0603 body, legible at 1400x1000. Non-polarised, terminals identical.

C2.why: view_top: silkscreen '10uF' immediately left of the can. Polarity NOT observable — the can renders as a plain cylinder with no band, and the silkscreen outline's chamfers are symmetric left to right.

R1.why: view_top: silkscreen '10K' beside the upper-left 0603. Resistor, terminals interchangeable.

R2.why: view_top: silkscreen '20K' beside its 0603. Unique value on this board, so the string cannot be misattributed.

R3.why: view_top: silkscreen '10K' beside the lower 0603. Shares its value string with R1, but both parts are 10K so the ambiguity costs nothing.

U1.why: No value in the source. Silkscreen prints 'KF301-5.0-2P', the part number, which is what makes the CONNECTOR type readable. No pin-1 marker on the body or the silk.

_refdes_note: No reference designator is printed on this board — the silkscreen carries VALUES (10K, 100nF, ...) and the KF301 part number. So refdes is false for every component and nothing anchors: under the component-refdes contract this case behaves exactly as before, which makes it the control.
